🧠 Crypto News Brief: Bitcoin holds near $64K as institutions quietly buy the dip through spot ETFs — yet a $100M+ Coldcard exploit and a looming Senate deadline keep the mood cautious. Resilient, but watchful. 🔓 Coldcard Exploit Losses Blow Past $100M Galaxy Research now attributes roughly 1,596 BTC — more than $100 million — to the ongoing Coldcard hardware-wallet exploit, spread across some 7,300 addresses, with a suspected fourth wave that could push losses toward $130 million. The flaw traces to a 2021 firmware change that weakened seed randomness, letting attackers rebuild keys without ever touching a device. Read full story 📉 First U.S. Spot Bitcoin ETF Set to Close Hashdex's DEFI, the smallest U.S. spot bitcoin fund, will make its final trade on August 17 before liquidating and returning cash to shareholders. Its exit stands in sharp contrast to a $77B-plus market led by BlackRock's IBIT, underscoring how concentrated ETF flows have become. More details 🏦 Bitcoin ETFs Open August With $170M Inflow U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs pulled in about $170 million to start the month, with BlackRock's IBIT capturing roughly $111 million and no fund posting an outflow. The buying arrived even as Italy's Intesa Sanpaolo disclosed it had trimmed its IBIT stake by nearly 94% last quarter. Read more 🌍 BTC and ETH Rise on Hormuz and Jobs-Report Hopes Both majors ticked higher, with Bitcoin holding around $64K, as traders weighed White House signals that Strait of Hormuz shipping could reopen and positioned ahead of Friday's July jobs report. Crypto stayed tightly correlated with equities, keeping macro firmly in the driver's seat. See details 🐂 BitMine's Ether Treasury Swells to $11.3B BitMine Immersion says it now holds about 5.8 million ETH — near 4.8% of all Ether in existence — alongside cash and strategic stakes worth $11.3 billion combined, cementing its position as the largest corporate Ether treasury. The firm has bought ETH every week since launching the strategy in mid-2025. Read full story 🔗 Ripple Deepens Tokenization Push on the XRP Ledger Ripple took equity stakes in UK firms ZILO and Licuido to bring regulated transfer-agency, issuance and collateral tools onto the XRP Ledger. Welcome back! Apple asked a judge for permission to send forensic experts through OpenAI's devices, and OpenAI answered in public instead of in court. Today also covers a training kernel Cursor gave away, the step where most agent projects quietly stall and a library running 70B models on a 4GB card.  In today's Atlas Newsletter: Apple: What exactly does it want from OpenAI's machines? Cursor: Why did a 2.37x kernel only produce a 1.41x gain? Agents: Where do most agent projects actually die? AirLLM: How do you fit 70B parameters on a 4GB GPU? Apple wants to open OpenAI's laptops Apple went to court Monday asking a judge to bar OpenAI and two former employees from touching anything it calls a trade secret.  It also asked for something bigger. Its lawyers and outside forensic experts want to inspect OpenAI's devices and accounts directly. OpenAI agreed to three of Apple's five conditions.  It refused the two that would let Apple search its machines. Apple says it now has serious concerns about eleven more OpenAI employees.  It also claims job candidates were told to bring Apple prototypes and CAD files to interviews for show and tell. Something else happened after the suit landed. Several former employees now at OpenAI reached out about returning Apple work devices they had kept. OpenAI fought back in public rather than in court. It called the suit careless and oddly personal, then published the email chain where Apple's own lawyers wrote to the wrong person after confusing two Asian last names, along with the apology that followed.
